metadata.description: Read the files attached to an Odoo record (read_attachment): printed text, or a scan transcribed

context.domain_knowledge:
# Files attached to a record (record_attachments)
A task, an invoice, a contact or any record can carry files (`ir.attachment`, by `res_model` and `res_id`). You **can read them**: the same reading the user gets when they drop a file in this chat. Printed text comes out page by page. A scanned PDF or a photo has no printed text: it is transcribed by this agent's own vision, once. `index_content` being empty says nothing: that is only Odoo's own extraction.
## How First find the files, as any other record::
atts = env['ir.attachment'].search([ ('res_model', '=', 'project.task'), ('res_id', '=', 42), ]) result = [{'id': a.id, 'name': a.name, 'mimetype': a.mimetype, 'file_size': a.file_size} for a in atts]
Then read one by its id. The text comes back to you, not to the user::
result = read_attachment(123) # the whole file result = read_attachment(123, page=2) # one page result = read_attachment(123, find='total') # the pages with those words
- The text stays on the conversation as a document: a later turn reads it with `read_document(name)` and nothing is transcribed twice. `documents()` lists what is kept. - Reading runs as the user. A file of a record they cannot open answers with a sentence saying so. Do not try another way. - A transcription of a scan takes a few seconds per file. Read the files the user asked about, not every file on the record. - "Digitize", "transcribe", "what does the attached PDF say", "read the scan": that is this helper. Then answer in prose, or with the figures they asked for.
## Hard rules - Do not say you cannot read a file before calling `read_attachment`. - Do not paste the whole transcription unless they asked for the text itself; answer the question with it. - When `read_attachment` says the file has no text that could be read, tell the user that, in one sentence, and stop.
